newsitem.title: USA: Temple-Inland sees paper demand improving.
newsitem.headline: Temple-Inland sees paper demand improving.

text.p: Temple-Inland Inc Chairmand and Chief Executive Officer Clifford Grum Friday said demand for the company's paper products is continuing to improve, which should lead to a restoration of margins as the year progresses.

In a statement accompanying Temple-Inland's fourth quarter financial results, the company said its paper group recorded fourth quarter operating earnings of $6.6 million, a 60 percent drop from the third quarter of 1996.
The company attributed the decline to higher energy costs, expenses associated with seasonal and maintenance downtime, and lower average prices for boxes.
For the fourth quarter, overall net income was $18.3 million or $0.33 a share, compared with $65 million or $1.16 a share in the year ago quarter. Revenues fell to $835.4 million from $868.8 million.

The company said it has consolidated its corrugated container and bleached paperboard operations into a single paper group, which reported 1996 operating earnings of $113.0 million, a decrease of 68 percent from 1995. The company said the group's corrugated container operation experienced declining prices during most of 1996.

Bolstered by stronger demand from both domestic and export markets, the overall demand picture improved in the second half of the year resulting in declining inventories and higher operating rates, Temple-Inland said.
However, the company said the improved demand scenario, however, has not yet resulted in price improvement for containerboard and boxes.
